text: The report identifies three growth-defect tiers across eight tested conditions; urea has severe defects for 97.9% of genes at ratio < 0.5, whereas quinate has 1.6% defective.
quote: The 8 carbon sources partition into demanding, moderate, and robust tiers based on the fraction of genes showing growth defects. Urea is the most demanding (97.9% of genes show severe defects at ratio < 0.5), while quinate is the most robust (only 1.6% defective). This tier structure is consistent across multiple thresholds.
heading: 1. Carbon sources define a three-tier essentiality landscape

text: The demanding tier comprises urea, acetate, and butanediol, with mean growth ratios of 0.41–0.65 and defects at ratio < 0.8 for 95–100% of genes.
quote: | Demanding | Urea, Acetate, Butanediol | 0.41–0.65 | 95–100% |
heading: 1. Carbon sources define a three-tier essentiality landscape

text: The moderate tier comprises asparagine and lactate, with mean growth ratios of 0.80–0.82 and defects at ratio < 0.8 for 37–45% of genes.
quote: | Moderate | Asparagine, Lactate | 0.80–0.82 | 37–45% |
heading: 1. Carbon sources define a three-tier essentiality landscape

text: The robust tier comprises glucarate, glucose, and quinate, with mean growth ratios of 1.25–1.36 and defects at ratio < 0.8 for 0.5–2.4% of genes.
quote: | Robust | Glucarate, Glucose, Quinate | 1.25–1.36 | 0.5–2.4% |
heading: 1. Carbon sources define a three-tier essentiality landscape

text: Principal component analysis of the 2,034×8 matrix requires five components to explain 82% of variance; PC1 explains 36.7%, while PC2 explains 12.7% and isolates urea with loading +0.75.
quote: PCA of the 2,034×8 growth matrix reveals that 5 principal components are needed to capture 82% of the variance. PC1 (36.7%) represents general growth sensitivity — all conditions load positively. PC2 (12.7%) isolates urea (loading = +0.75), separating nitrogen metabolism from carbon metabolism. The remaining PCs distinguish specific carbon source pairs.
heading: 2. Conditions are largely independent — 5 PCs capture 82% of variance

text: Across all 28 condition pairs, median Pearson r is 0.25 and the maximum is 0.58 for acetate–butanediol; the report interprets the eight conditions as providing approximately five phenotypic dimensions.
quote: Pairwise Pearson correlations between conditions are moderate at best (highest: acetate–butanediol, r = 0.58; median across all 28 pairs: r = 0.25). This means the 8 conditions provide approximately 5 independent dimensions of phenotypic information — far more than the 2-group (demanding vs robust) model would suggest.
heading: 2. Conditions are largely independent — 5 PCs capture 82% of variance

text: Hierarchical clustering gives K = 3 but a low silhouette score of 0.24; its two large groups contain 1,160 and 850 genes, and no specific functional enrichment survives false-discovery-rate correction.
quote: Hierarchical clustering of genes by their 8-condition growth profiles produces an optimal K = 3 with a low silhouette score (0.24). The two large modules (1,160 and 850 genes) represent broad "generally sensitive" vs "generally tolerant" groups without any specific functional enrichment surviving FDR correction. This indicates that gene essentiality varies continuously across conditions rather than falling into discrete functional categories.
heading: 3. The phenotype landscape is a continuum, not discrete modules

text: A 24-gene aromatic-degradation module is the reported exception to the continuous phenotype landscape, with mean quinate z-score −7.28 and near-zero mean scores in other conditions.
quote: The one exception is a small module of 24 genes with extreme quinate-specific defects (mean z-score = -7.28 on quinate, near-zero on other conditions). These are the aromatic degradation pathway genes, which form the only discrete phenotypic module in the dataset.
heading: 3. The phenotype landscape is a continuum, not discrete modules

text: 625 genes (31%) have condition-specificity score ≥ 1.0, indicating concentrated growth importance in one tested condition.
quote: 625 genes (31%) have a condition specificity score ≥ 1.0, meaning their growth importance is concentrated on one carbon source. The top condition-specific genes for each carbon source correspond precisely to the expected metabolic pathways:

text: The 51-gene quinate-specific set at spec > 0.5 and z < −1 includes Complex I subunits beyond the core pathway; the proposed electron-transport demand is an inference. PQQ-biosynthesis genes are specific to both quinate and glucose.
quote: The quinate-specific gene set (51 genes at spec > 0.5, z < -1) extends beyond the core degradation pathway to include NADH-ubiquinone oxidoreductase subunits (Complex I), suggesting that aromatic catabolism places unique demands on the electron transport chain. PQQ biosynthesis genes appear as condition-specific for both quinate and glucose, consistent with PQQ-dependent dehydrogenases catalyzing the first step of both pathways.

The 313 uncertain-class genes are even more distinctive: 361 bp mean length, 42% annotated, 31% core — consistent with gene fragments or pseudogenes rather than true essential genes.

text: The complete matrix has 2,034 genes measured in eight conditions. Ratios are mutant/wild-type; values > 1.0 can reflect normalization rather than a true advantage. Mean ratios range 3.3-fold, from 0.41 on urea to 1.36 on quinate.
quote: The complete growth matrix consists of 2,034 genes with growth ratio measurements on all 8 carbon sources. Growth ratios represent mutant/wild-type ratios, where values < 1.0 indicate growth defects and values > 1.0 indicate no defect (or slight growth advantage due to experimental normalization). The conditions span a 3.3-fold range in mean growth ratio (0.41 for urea to 1.36 for quinate).
heading: Growth Matrix Structure

text: Across tested cluster counts k = 2–25, the silhouette score is low (0.24), supporting a gradient rather than well-separated gene-response modules.
quote: The low silhouette score (0.24) across all tested k values (2–25) indicates that the phenotypic landscape lacks natural cluster boundaries. Most genes vary gradually in their condition sensitivity rather than falling into discrete response groups. This is consistent with Guzman et al. (2018)'s proposal that essentiality is a continuous variable — our data shows this continuity manifests as a gradient across conditions, not as discrete functional modules.
heading: Module Structure vs Gradient

text: The report contrasts its lack of discrete ADP1 modules, apart from the 24-gene quinate module, with published E. coli chemical-genetic modules; differing perturbation methods or organismal architecture are proposed, not established, explanations.
quote: - Nichols et al. (2011) found that chemical-genetic profiles in *E. coli* define "phenotypic modules" extending beyond operon boundaries. We do NOT find discrete modules in ADP1 — only a continuous gradient with one exception (the 24-gene quinate module). This may reflect differences between single-gene deletions (this study) and chemical perturbations (Nichols et al.), or may indicate that ADP1's metabolic architecture is more interconnected than *E. coli*'s.
heading: Literature Context

text: This analysis uses single-gene deletions rather than transposon sequencing; the report compares its 625 condition-specific genes with findings from RB-TnSeq.
quote: - Wetmore et al. (2015) demonstrated that RB-TnSeq across diverse conditions identifies condition-specific gene functions. Our analysis uses single-gene deletions rather than TnSeq, but reaches the same conclusion: condition-specific phenotyping dramatically increases the functional annotation yield. The 625 condition-specific genes include many with known functions that would not be detected on a single carbon source.
heading: Literature Context

text: Growth ratios come from single-timepoint measurements with unknown technical noise, and condition-specificity results assume cross-condition differences are biological.
quote: - Growth ratios are single-timepoint measurements with unknown technical noise. The condition specificity analysis assumes that variation across conditions reflects biology, not measurement error.
heading: Limitations

quote: - The complete matrix (2,034 genes) excludes essential genes (499) and genes with incomplete data (316), biasing toward dispensable genes with successful deletion mutants.
heading: Limitations

text: Only eight conditions were tested; the approximately five inferred independent dimensions may increase with a broader panel.
quote: - Only 8 carbon sources were tested. The ~5 independent dimensions may increase with more conditions.
